subject: Deal-linked GPU provisioning + staged migration sprint plan
summary: Mutual action plan for provisioning dedicated GPU capacity tied to Brightleaf Labs commitment. Includes sizing assumptions, staging/canary windows, procurement steps, and final cutover acceptance criteria.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Park <alex@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Deal-linked GPU provisioning + staged migration sprint plan

Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I put together a compact mutual-action plan for the hosted->dedicated migration tied to your committed throughput. The attached sizing-assumptions.xlsx and MAP_v1.pdf show the workload profile we used and a proposed sprint timeline. Highlights: 

- Sizing assumptions (baseline): 120 QPS peak, 1.2k avg tokens/request, working set fits into 24GB KV for preferred model variant.
- Concurrency target for P95 < 300ms, P99 SLO 450ms for inference.
- Estimated reserved capacity: 6x A100-40GB equiv nodes (quantized variant) with staging pool of 1 node for canary.
- Lead time: GPU commissioning estimate 3–4 weeks from signed commitment + procurement approval.
- Cutover approach: 3-phase (staging smoke, canary 5% traffic, full swap).

Proposed cutover windows (pick one):
  1) Sat 2026-05-09 02:00–06:00 PT (low traffic)
  2) Tue 2026-05-12 01:00–05:00 PT
  3) Sun 2026-05-17 03:00–07:00 PT

Asks:
- Confirm which window you prefer.
- Approval to open procurement request (we’ll use the proc flow in the attached document).
- Alignment call Tuesday 2026-04-13 10:00 PT to freeze final sizing and acceptance criteria.

I put Karthik on Cc for capacity-side commitments and Ben for operational runbook sanity check.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sizing-assumptions.xlsx (spreadsheet), MAP_v1.pdf (mutual action plan)

From: Alex Park <alex@brightleaf.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Danielle Shaw <danielle@brightleaf.ai>
Date: 2026-04-11T11:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deal-linked GPU provisioning + staged migration sprint plan

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear plan and the assumptions doc. Quick clarifications before we lock a window: 

1) The 120 QPS peak was conservative — on our side we run spikes up to ~150 QPS for short bursts. Can your sizing absorb 150 QPS with the same latency SLO if we hold bursts to <5 minutes?
2) How disruptive is the canary phase to live traffic routing? We prefer an approach that leaves the hosted API as the fallback for any degradation.
3) Procurement lead time internally is usually 2 weeks once we sign — so your 3–4 week estimate for GPU commissioning sounds fine but we will try to compress our approval.

Preferred window: option 1 (Sat 2026-05-09) or option 3 if option 1 conflicts with your ops schedule.

Let me know if you want me to loop in our infra lead (we can add them to the alignment call).

—Alex
Alex Park
Head of Product, Brightleaf Labs
alex@brightleaf.ai

Marissa / Ben —

Couple operational notes from capacity planning: 

- If Brightleaf spikes to 150 QPS for short bursts, we can handle it by allowing short token-burst headroom and autoscaling burst lanes, but that requires we reserve an extra 1 node in the pool (i.e., 7 nodes total committed) for 48 hours after cutover to absorb initial traffic variability. If they agree to cap bursts at 5 min we can auto-throttle to protect latency SLOs.
- Commissioning timeline (detailed):
   * Week 0: Procurement + PO sign (customer/Redwood legal & billing finalization)
   * Week 1–2: Provision reserved instances in region (image bake, kernel tuning)
   * Week 3: Staging validation and prefix/KV warm-up; perf regression tests
- Procurement request doc attached. Need Marissa to confirm we can start PO as soon as the SOW is signed. Also need internal infra ticket to pre-reserve one staging GPU in our shared cluster for smoke tests (I’ll open RID-1459).

Action items: 
- Marissa: confirm preferred cutover window and push DocuSign link to them so PO can start.
- Ben: please validate canary runbook and acceptance gates (I skimmed, looks fine; see canary-runbook.md).
- Karthik: I’ll coordinate provisioning schedule with infra ops and flag any blockers by 2026-04-20.

Karthik
Head of Capacity, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: procurement-request.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Alex Park <alex@brightleaf.ai>
Date: 2026-04-13T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deal-linked GPU provisioning + staged migration sprint plan

Quick runbook notes from an ops perspective — high level canary acceptance criteria: 

1) Canary (5% traffic) must sustain P95 latency < 320ms and no more than 0.5% error rate for 30 min.
2) KV warm-up must reach 90% hit ratio before moving beyond canary.
3) Auto-fallback to hosted API should be wired through a route-level failover (route -> hosted-backend) with circuit-breaker at 10% error uplift.
4) Rollback procedure: immediate traffic switchback (DNS/Traf) + drain nodes for 15 min, then a post-mortem within 24 hours.

I’ll publish a short canary-runbook.md and add step-by-step console actions. For the staging GPU you’ll want us to run a smoke traffic profile (I can script that).

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: canary-runbook.md
